papers.title: A wedge-complement domain with a nonstarlike Cassinian ball
papers.abstract:
U = C minus the closed wedge {u>=1, |v|<=(u-1)/20} is an open connected proper planar domain, starlike about 0 in both the ordinary and the strict boundary-point sense, yet its Cassinian ball B_c(0,7/4) contains 4+i and omits the midpoint 2+i/2. Klen-Mohapatra-Sahoo Conjecture 4.7 (every Cassinian ball in a starlike domain is starlike about the centre) is false for every n>=2 reading posed in the plane, under both the ordinary and the strict domain hypotheses.

papers.title: All corrected odd-open and even-closed XOR-magic degrees at powers of two
papers.abstract:

papers.title: An adverse non-Q graph from the cyclic Latin square of order six
papers.abstract:
The cyclic Latin square graph of order 6 (cells of Z6xZ6 adjacent when sharing a row, column or symbol) has lambda_min = -3 and upsilon = 6, both unchanged after deleting every open neighbourhood, and no isolated vertices, so it is adverse; its stability number is 5 by the transversal parity obstruction, so it is not a Q-graph. This refutes Cardoso-Luz Conjecture 4.2 (survey arXiv:1811.05516, Optimization 69(1) 2020) that all adverse graphs are Q-graphs, also under the JCO 2016 'non complete' reading.

papers.title: A clique with a five-edge tail reverses the hubs-biased Kirchhoff ordering
papers.abstract:
Estrada-Mugnolo (J. Math. Anal. Appl. 507 (2022) 125728, arXiv:2101.07103) Conjecture 4.13 asserts R_1 >= R_0 >= R_-1 for hubs-biased Kirchhoff indices, with equality iff regular. papers.title: A parity-corrected potential proves the Elsholtz–Klahn–Lipnik four-term progression-free digit-set conjecture
papers.abstract:
Elsholtz-Klahn-Lipnik (Des. Codes Cryptogr. 91 (2023) 1443-1452, arXiv:2211.02588) Conjecture 2.4, repeated as Conjecture 4.6 in Lipnik's 2023 thesis: for every prime p >= 13, p = 1 mod 4, and every n divisible by (p+3)/2, S(D,n) with D = {0..(p-1)/2,(p+3)/2} has no nonconstant 4-term AP. Proved uniformly (primality unnecessary) via E(t) = 4t^2 - (3p-5)(-1)^t: the only wrapped coordinate progressions are (h-3,0,h,3) and (3,h,0,h-3), with gap 16; ordinary progressions have gap 16 s^2; equal digit frequencies force every gap to vanish.

papers.title: No order-15 circulant has diameter 2 and monophonic position number 2
papers.abstract:
Tuite-Thomas-Chandran (arXiv:2106.06827v3; Ars Math. Contemp. 2025) Conjecture 4.5 asserts that for every n >= 11 there is a circulant graph of order n with diameter 2 and monophonic position number 2 (still listed as open in the survey arXiv:2501.19385 v5, August 2026). False at the interior order 15. Every diameter-2 circulant of order 15 contains a triangle, or is C5[3K1] (jumps {1,4,6} or {2,3,7}) with three open twins; both kinds of triple are mp-sets. Verified circulant examples exist at every other order 11..40 (supplementary; not claimed beyond).

papers.title: A cubic counterexample to edge-pattern convex domination
papers.abstract:
Pirot-Sereni (arXiv:1904.05618; SIAM J. Discrete Math. 35(4) (2021) 2815-2843) Conjecture 2, also Conjecture 1.5.1 of Pirot's 2019 thesis, is false at d = 3, r = 2. The 8-vertex edge-rooted pattern P (root edge 01; edges 01,02,03,15,17,34,46,56: a 6-cycle with two pendants) is 3-regular, of exact depth 2 and girth 6, with e(P) = (2/5,14/5,4/5). So no convex combination of tree constraints is weaker than e(P). The source's optimized bounds (Lemma 10) are unaffected.

papers.title: Two hook tableaux of size 12 with equal multisets of 8-minors: the k+4 reconstruction conjecture fails
papers.abstract:
Erickson-Herden-Meddaugh-Sepanski-Hammon-Mohn-Ruiz-Bolanos (arXiv:2307.13161; J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 209 (2025) 105950), Conjecture conj:k+4: for n >= k+4 the multiset mM_k(T) of k-minors (over all jeu de taquin deletion sequences) determines a standard Young tableau. False at k = 8, n = 12. The hooks T1 (first row 1 5 7 8 12) and T2 (first row 1 2 3 7 10 11) are distinct and have identical mM_8 (19,958,400 minors each). Supplementary (ordinary mathematics, not Lean): a hook weight formula shows that no bound n >= k + c works for any constant c, with an explicit n = k+5 failure at k = 11.
